races.title: State Senate, District 18
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Steve Padilla
cands.bio: California State Senator for District 18 since December 2022. Former Chula Vista police detective (13 years). Served on the Chula Vista City Council (1994–2002, 2016–2022) and as Mayor of Chula Vista (2002–2006). Has served on the California Coastal Commission.

controversies.text: While Chula Vista's mayor, Padilla had a personal bodyguard paid by the city, at a base pay of $10,000 a month. Critics objected during his 2006 re-election bid, which he lost. In 2014 he said he hired the bodyguard after anonymous threats. He said it was cheaper than using police, and he called it a mistake.

endorsements.text: Democratic Party of California (2026 Senate race)
California Federation of Labor Unions, AFL-CIO (2026 Senate race)

cands.gaps: We could not read the text of the news articles on his campaign site about data-center utility costs, so we have no verified detail on his data-center bills. Wikipedia says only that he has introduced bills regulating computing hubs and data centers, with no bill numbers or dates, and describes no ban or moratorium. We found no documented actions or statements from him on homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land purchases, H-1B or immigration enforcement, gun policy, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys, so his own stated positions in 2026 are thin. His 2014 campaign themes and his 2002 mayoral platform are the only stated positions we found. We found no foreign-government ties.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia says he was born in San Diego and lives in Chula Vista, and Wikipedia says his mother bought a home in Chula Vista to raise the family and he graduated from Bonita Vista High School in 1985.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: State Senator since 2022; Chula Vista City Council member 1994–2002 and 2016–2022; Mayor of Chula Vista 2002–2006; Chula Vista police officer and detective for 13 years; helped move the city to two-year budget cycles.
qual.why: He has held legislative office at both city and state level, including a state Senate seat since 2022, and has a public-safety career and public administration degree, which fits a role that writes law and the budget.
qual.label: He has held legislative office at both city and state level, including a state Senate seat since 2022, and has a public-safety career and public administration degree, which fits a role that writes law and the budget.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: In his 2002 mayoral campaign he proposed requiring developers to pay for roads and public services before their developments are approved, to address traffic congestion from the city's rapid growth.

back-police-order.evidence: In his 2014 City Council campaign he said he would strengthen public safety by giving law enforcement and first responders the resources they need.

cands.name: Art Hodges
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Senate District 18 in 2026. By his campaign's account, he is a Bishop overseeing about 350 churches in Southern California and has been a pastor for 40 years. He says he was previously a school principal and a college chancellor. He has not held elected office.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Art Hodges was born or when he moved to Southern California. His jobs, the institutions he led and the dates are not documented beyond his campaign website. His claim that he won two U.S. Supreme Court rulings on reopening houses of worship is not backed by any independent source we have. We found no independent news coverage of him. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. We found no documented positions on data centers, development, property taxes, housing ownership, immigration or H-1B, gun policy, policing, or school choice and teacher pay.

local.label: Roots 90: His campaign website says he was raised in Southern California since infancy and that his children and grandchildren live in Chula Vista; his birthplace is not stated.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: By his own account he has worked as a school principal, college chancellor, pastor for 40 years and Bishop overseeing hundreds of churches and ministers, and has served as a CEO. He has held no elected or legislative office.
qual.why: Long management and organizational leadership roles put him in the middle range, but there is no legislative, budget or policy work on record, and the details come only from his campaign site. Board seats were not counted.
